title: Real-time geometric complexity of language is associated with global functioning across psychosis and major depression.
summary: For picture descriptions from 129 German-speaking participants, LLM embedding dynamics were associated with clinical dimensions across depression, schizophrenia-spectrum and control groups. The strongest reported association was with global functioning, for which the measures explained 51% of variance; this observational association is not a diagnostic or causal result.
ai_technology: Geometric complexity of real-time speech embeddings
organization: University of Basel; LMU Munich; University of Lübeck; University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf; University of Groningen; University of Zurich

evidence.tested: For picture descriptions from 129 German-speaking participants, LLM embedding dynamics were associated with clinical dimensions across depression, schizophrenia-spectrum and control groups. The strongest reported association was with global functioning, for which the measures explained 51% of variance; this observational association is not a diagnostic or causal result.
evidence.unknown: The study evaluates the reported models and datasets only; broader generalization and real-world deployment outcomes were not established.
evidence.ai_role: German BERT converts spontaneous speech into contextual embeddings; geometric measures of their temporal dynamics are modeled against clinical functioning and symptom scores.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
